newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea-related credit unions in Osaka to merge.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea-related credit unions in Osaka to merge.

text.p: The Osaka government said on Wednesday that five North Korea-related credit unions in Japan will merge into a single institution and take over the operations of the troubled Chogin Osaka Shinyo Kumiai.

Unrecoverable loans at Chogin Osaka, which like the other five credit unions is run by North Korean residents in Japan, are estimated at 200 billion yen based on the Osaka prefectural government's financial assessment, Osaka officials said in a statement.

The Osaka government will ask the Deposit Insurance Corp of Japan (DIC), charged with protecting depositors from failures at financial institutions, to buy any problem loans held by Chogin Osaka, it said.
It said Chogin Osaka's problem loans ballooned after the burst of Japan's asset bubble in 1990 and the subsequent slowdown in the economy.
